audit.whatIsWrong: The Equalizer is described as a channel and as impassable ground: 'respect the cast, don't charge in during the channel' (spikes[1]), and 'if he drops it on your intended path you cannot walk through it to stack him. Let the Equalizer channel happen, dodge perpendicular, then re-engage after it ends' (mid).
audit.why: The Equalizer is not a channel — Rumble fires the rockets and is free to act immediately. And it creates a burning line that damages and slows; it does not block movement. A Tahm Kench told he cannot cross it will stand off the wave for five seconds waiting out an ability he could have walked through, which in a matchup he wins 57.55% is the difference between a kill and a reset. Walking a tank with grey-health recovery through a damage-and-slow line to reach a Rumble who has no hard CC is frequently the correct play.
audit.corrected: The Equalizer damages and slows; it does not block your path and there is no channel to wait out. Cross it if the trade on the far side is worth the burn — you are the tank in this matchup.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (R The Equalizer: 'creating a wall of flames that damages and slows enemies')

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon's magic resist shred is never mentioned anywhere in the entry, in either layer's prose.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon reduces the target's Magic Resist, carries two charges, and reloads on a 0.5s recast at 850 range. That is the mechanical reason Rumble threatens a tank at all: he removes the exact stat you buy to answer him, and he can apply the shred twice before you close from 850 to Tongue Lash's 900. The full layer's own tldr already tells the player to 'build MR' without ever explaining that Rumble deletes it.
audit.corrected: Electro Harpoon shreds your MR and carries two charges — the debuff is why his Flamespitter hurts a tank. Close the gap before he lands both.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers name Scrap Shield as the cooldown to track: full breakdown.cooldowns says 'Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining', dosFull[0] says 'Track Rumble's Scrap Shield before you commit', and wants.you[0] says to punish 'when his Scrap Shield is on cooldown'.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a 6-second cooldown. It is never meaningfully down, so building a game plan around tracking it produces a player who waits for a window that arrives constantly and means nothing. The real gate is the Heat bar: at 100% Heat Rumble Overheats and cannot cast spells at all for a few seconds — no Scrap Shield, no Harpoon, no Flamespitter. That is a hard lockout on a champion with no hard CC in his kit, and it is the only window in the matchup worth naming.
audit.corrected: Track the Heat bar, not Scrap Shield's 6 seconds. Overheat locks him out of every spell — walk in, stack, stun, Devour.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (P Junkyard Titan, W Scrap Shield cd 6)

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] has Rumble deliberately overheating as an offensive plan: 'Run Flamespitter through you at close range and overheat to deal bonus damage before you reach 3 stacks'.
audit.why: Overheat does grant attack speed and bonus on-hit damage, so this is not simply false — but it is framed as a win condition when it is the one state Rumble genuinely fears in this matchup. A Rumble stuck at 100% Heat next to a Tahm Kench cannot shield, cannot slow, and cannot disengage. Presenting it as his goal teaches the reader to back off at exactly the moment he should be walking forward.
audit.corrected: Rumble wants Danger Zone at 50% Heat, not Overheat at 100% — he wants the empowered abilities without the spell lockout.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Rumble has no hard CC.
audit.why: Rumble's whole kit contains one slow (Electro Harpoon) and one slowing zone (The Equalizer). There is no stun, root, knockup or displacement anywhere in it. Against a 900-range Tongue Lash and a 1000-1200 Abyssal Dive that is decisive: once the Harpoon charges are spent there is physically nothing stopping Tahm Kench from closing. This is the reason for the 57.55% and it is never said.
audit.corrected: Rumble has no hard CC at all — only the Harpoon slow. Spend those two charges and he cannot stop you walking him down.

audit.whatIsWrong: late calls Flamespitter a channel: 'a full Flamespitter run barely moves your real HP bar if you activate E as the channel ends'.
audit.why: Flamespitter is a 3-second cone that Rumble casts and then moves, attacks and casts through. Treating it as a channel with an end to time against gives the player a cue that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Flamespitter burns for 3 seconds while he moves freely — time Thick Skin off the burn expiring, not off a channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing-interactions.json proposes a knockup-enabler line for this pairing: 'Both sides carry displacement (Abyssal Dive (W) vs Scrap Shield (W))'.
audit.why: Scrap Shield has no displacement. It is a shield plus a move-speed burst; the knockup and terrain flags on it in the kit file are derived-flag false positives, and Riot's own description confirms it. I did not write this line, and it should not be applied for any owner in this pairing.
audit.corrected: Do not add a displacement-race line here — only Tahm Kench has a knockup.
sources: champ-data/_kits/rumble.json (W Scrap Shield description vs flags)

edits.after: Rumble's Equalizer damages and slows but does not block ground — if the trade on the far side is worth the burn, walk straight through it.

edits.after: Rumble's Flamespitter + Electro Harpoon combo goes online — the Harpoon shreds your MR twice over, and that is what makes his burn hurt a tank.

edits.after: The Equalizer is a damage-and-slow line, not a wall — it costs you health to cross, never the path itself, so cross it when three An Acquired Taste stacks are worth the burn.

edits.before: Rumble has no mobility to escape once his Scrap Shield is on cooldown; your 3-stack Tongue Lash stun into Devour punishes every overheat and Thick Skin lets you absorb his burst to reach the lockdown.
edits.after: Rumble carries no hard CC at all — one Harpoon slow and nothing else — so once both charges are spent there is nothing between you and him, and Overheat hands you a free spell-less target.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your reclaim window. Rumble's kill threat only exists when he is near overheat and has his Scrap Shield up; once those are burned he is a melee-range mage with no escape and your stacks are already on him. Tongue Lash to slow, walk forward for the third stack, stun, then Devour — he cannot reposition out of that sequence without burning Flash. At Level 6 the dynamic inverts hard: Rumble's Equalizer is the best zoning tool in this matchup, and if he drops it on your intended path you cannot walk through it to stack him. Let the Equalizer channel happen, dodge perpendicular, then re-engage after it ends rather than tanking the full AOE duration.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your reclaim window. Rumble's kill threat lives entirely in his Heat bar and his two Harpoon charges; spend both and he is a melee-range mage with no hard CC in his kit and your stacks already on him. Tongue Lash to slow, walk forward for the third stack, stun, then Devour — he cannot reposition out of that sequence without Flash. At Level 6 respect The Equalizer's damage, not its geometry: it burns and slows, it does not block ground, so it costs you health to cross and never the path itself. Cross it when three stacks and a Devour are on the other side; sidestep it when they are not.

edits.before: Two completed tank items and you are the attrition nightmare Rumble cannot solve. His Flamespitter AP damage is high in a vacuum, but Thick Skin grey-health at 2 items means a full Flamespitter run barely moves your real HP bar if you activate E as the channel ends, and your 3-stack Devour removes him from any fight entirely for the duration. Peel your ADC, walk at Rumble with Tongue Lash baiting the Equalizer early in the teamfight, then Devour him the moment his overheat expires — he contributes zero damage while swallowed and his team loses its primary AOE threat for the fight window.
edits.after: Two completed tank items and you are the attrition nightmare Rumble cannot solve. His Flamespitter AP damage is high in a vacuum, but Flamespitter burns for three seconds while he moves freely — time Thick Skin off the burn expiring and it barely moves your real HP bar. Watch his Heat: the moment it tips to 100% he cannot cast anything for a few seconds, and that is your stun into Devour. Peel your ADC, bait The Equalizer out early in the fight, and remember that his two Harpoon charges shredding your MR are what make a magic resist item look thin.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rumble Heat bar: matchup-defining — 100% Overheats him out of every spell for seconds. Scrap Shield is only 6s, do not track it. - Two Harpoon charges shred MR. - Devour: kill windows only.

edits.before: Rumble wins by landing Scrap Shield, denying your pattern, and kiting you off the wave.
edits.after: Rumble wins by shredding your MR with Harpoon and kiting you off the wave from 850.

notes: _missing-interactions.json's knockup-enabler row for tahmkench/rumble and rumble/tahmkench is built on a bad derived flag — Scrap Shield carries knockup and terrain flags in champ-data/_kits/rumble.json that its own Riot description contradicts ('pulls up a shield, protecting him from damage and granting him a quick burst of speed'). Any owner applying that row will publish a displacement that does not exist. Same false-positive pattern puts a terrain flag on The Equalizer, which is what the original text was built on. Worth a sweep of the derived flags before other slices consume those rows. The full layer's tldr for this matchup claims '%HP DoT' for Rumble; the kit file sets no percentHealth flag on Flamespitter and its description does not mention max-health scaling, so I left it alone rather than assert either way — flagging it as unverified.
